title: Punishment for Murder
chapter: Chapter VI: Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
summary: Prescribes punishment for whoever commits murder.
fullText: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Where a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other ground, each member of such group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainExplanation: Deals with the crime of intentionally causing death of another person. It carries the highest penal consequences including life imprisonment or capital punishment, with specific new provisions addressing mob lynching.
punishment: Death or Imprisonment for Life, and fine.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: Theft
chapter: Chapter XVII: Of Offences Against Property
summary: Defines theft of movable property and prescribes punishment.
fullText: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft. Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and in case of second or subsequent conviction, with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and with fine.
plainExplanation: Applies when someone dishonestly takes someone else's movable belongings (like a phone, vehicle, or wallet) without their permission.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; enhanced for repeat offenses. Community service for petty theft under ₹5,000 upon return.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property
chapter: Chapter XVII: Of Offences Against Property
summary: Defines cheating and penalizes deceitful inducement causing wrongful loss or wrongful delivery of property.
fullText: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person... commits cheating. Subsection (4): Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainExplanation: Covers fraud, UPI scams, fake investment schemes, online shopping deceit, or misleading someone to transfer money or property under false pretenses.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
compoundable: Compoundable with permission of the court
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: Cheating by Personation
chapter: Chapter XVII: Of Offences Against Property
summary: Penalizes cheating by pretending to be some other person or substituting one person for another.
fullText: A person is said to cheat by personation if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is. Punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or with fine, or with both.
plainExplanation: Applies when someone creates a fake profile, impersonates a bank official, celebrity, or friend on social media (Instagram, WhatsApp) to scam or extract confidential information.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: Criminal Intimidation
chapter: Chapter XIX: Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
summary: Penalizes threatening any person with injury to person, reputation, or property with intent to cause alarm.
fullText: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do... commits criminal intimidation. If threat be to cause death or grievous hurt, imprisonment may extend to seven years.
plainExplanation: Applies when someone sends threatening messages online or in person, threatens to leak private photos, cause physical harm, or ruin reputation unless demands are met.
punishment: Simple intimidation: up to 2 years or fine or both; Threat of death/grievous hurt/extortion: up to 7 years and fine.
cognizable: Non-Cognizable (general) / Cognizable (aggravated threats in certain jurisdictions)
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: Stalking
chapter: Chapter V: Of Offences Against Women and Children
summary: Penalizes physical or electronic monitoring and following of a woman causing distress or apprehension.
fullText: Any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest, or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking.
plainExplanation: Covers cyberstalking, relentless messaging, tracking someone's online activities on Instagram/social apps, or repeated unwanted advances after being told to stop.
punishment: First conviction: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine; Subsequent conviction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: Criminal Breach of Trust
chapter: Chapter XVII: Of Offences Against Property
summary: Dishonest misappropriation or conversion to own use of property entrusted to a person.
fullText: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law... commits criminal breach of trust.
plainExplanation: Applicable in tenancy disputes where a landlord dishonestly withholds a refundable security deposit without legal justification, or an agent misuses entrusted funds.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)
